Ra High School makes history with first men’s netball team at nationals
item.description: Ra High School has made history by sending its first-ever men’s netball team to the Crest Chicken Secondary School Championship, after a journey shaped by determination, sacrifice and strong community support. Coach Aloisio Nakewa says seeing the team compete at the national level is a proud moment for the players, the school and the wider Ra community.
item.content:encoded:
Ra High School has made history by sending its first-ever men’s netball team to the Crest Chicken Secondary School Championship, after a journey shaped by determination, sacrifice and strong community support.

Coach Aloisio Nakewa says seeing the team compete at the national level is a proud moment for the players, the school and the wider Ra community.

The man from Ra, who is in his second year coaching at the school, says the journey has not been easy, with the team facing challenges including fundraising for transport, uniforms and other equipment.

Nakewa says when the players first started training, they had to learn the basics of preparing themselves for competition, including having the right gear and understanding the demands of the sport.

He says the players’ commitment, willingness to learn and dedication during training helped them improve and qualify through the Western Rally.

In their first national appearance, Ra High School went down 14-7 to defending champions Yat Sen Secondary School.

Despite the result, Nakewa says the tournament is an important learning experience for the players as they continue to develop men’s netball at the school.

He says the team’s goal was to perform well, gain valuable experience and test themselves against some of the best school teams in the country.

Nakewa, who previously played for the Ra Netball Association men’s team, says being part of the national competition has also been a learning experience for him as a coach.

He says the support from families, friends and the Ra community has motivated the players as they represent their school for the first time.

For the young Ra High School players, this tournament is more than just a competition, it marks the beginning of a new chapter for men’s netball at the school.

The Crest Chicken Secondary School Championship will continue tomorrow, with the finals on Friday.

item.title: Secondary Schools Football: Guru Nanak secures 3-0 win over Ratu Navula
item.description: Shree Guru Nanak Khalsa College produced a dominant second-half performance to defeat Ratu Navula College 3–0 in an exciting Extra Supermarket Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association Championship 2026 Under-19 match at Subrail Park in Labasa. After a goalless first half, Guru Nanak stepped up in the second half with better attacking play, sharp passing and strong teamwork to secure three valua
item.content:encoded:
Shree Guru Nanak Khalsa College produced a dominant second-half performance to defeat Ratu Navula College 3–0 in an exciting Extra Supermarket Fiji Secondary Schools Football Association Championship 2026 Under-19 match at Subrail Park in Labasa.

After a goalless first half, Guru Nanak stepped up in the second half with better attacking play, sharp passing and strong teamwork to secure three valuable points.

Coach Raiyaz Khan praised his players for their teamwork and discipline, saying the boys played a brilliant game and followed the team’s plan throughout the match.

Khan also praised the performance of his midfielders, saying they played an important role in controlling the game and creating goal-scoring opportunities.

He also reflected on their opening match against Vunimono High School, describing it as a tough encounter, with Guru Nanak earning a draw to collect one point.

With the win over Ratu Navula College, the school now has four points from its opening two matches.

Khan says the team’s ultimate goal is clear, which is to win the Under-19 title.

Meanwhile, in the Under-15 category, Nadi Sangam College and AD Patel Secondary School played out a goalless draw , with both teams creating chances but failing to score.

Nadi Sangam College coach Rahil Singh says it was a tough match, but he was proud of the effort shown by his players.

Singh says the team needs to improve its build-up play, create more scoring chances and work on finishing in front of goal.

He says Nadi Sangam College is aiming to end a 20-year wait for a title, with their last championship win coming in 2006.

Singh says bringing the title back to Nadi Sangam College is the team’s dream this season.

He also thanked the fans and players for their support and effort.

item.title: Navatu Secondary U19 team creates history but the job is not over
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 19/08/2026 The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has created history as the first northern team to book a place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final, but the job is not yet over.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 19/08/2026

The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has created history as the first northern team to book a place in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final, but the job is not yet over.

Speaking to the players after their historic win over Ratu Kadavulevu School last weekend, head coach Alipate Ravulo says they had achieved what they had set out to do and should now be ready for the next challenge.

He says they should always stay grounded and start from zero again, rather than putting themselves on a pedestal.

Ravulo adds that nothing has changed in terms of the goal they want to achieve.

He also acknowledged the hard work and determination shown by the players, as well as the support from their parents and the Vanua.

A new champion will be crowned in the Under-19 grade after defending champions Nasinu Secondary School fell to Ratu Navula College 30-25 in the quarter-final.

Navatu Secondary School will face Lelean Memorial School at 2.20pm at the HFC Bank Stadium.

In the other Deans finals, Ratu Navula College will take on QVS at 8am in the Under-14 grade, followed by RKS facing Marist Brothers High School in the Under-15 grade at 9.05am.

Suva Grammar School will meet RKS at 12.50pm in the Under-17 grade, while Grammar will face Lelean at 6.10pm in the Under-18 grade.

In the Weet-Bix Raluve finals, Nasinu Secondary School will play Saint Vincent College at 10.25am, while Lomary Secondary School will meet MGM High School at 5.05pm.

All games will be played at the HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Inoke Ravuiwasa signs with Fijian Drua for 2027 Super Rugby Pacific Season
item.description: Experienced tighthead prop Inoke Ravuiwasa has signed with the Fijian Drua for the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season. The Drua says they have secured the services of the proven domestic performer, who brings significant experience from Fiji’s provincial rugby, Fiji Police rugby, the Fijian Warriors and Australia’s John I Dent Cup.
item.content:encoded:
Experienced tighthead prop Inoke Ravuiwasa has signed with the Fijian Drua for the 2027 Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific season.

The Drua says they have secured the services of the proven domestic performer, who brings significant experience from Fiji’s provincial rugby, Fiji Police rugby, the Fijian Warriors and Australia’s John I Dent Cup.

Originally from Tavuki, Taveuni, Ravuiwasa most recently represented Suva in the Skipper Cup and also featured for the Skipper Select against the Drua during their 2026 pre-season trial.

The 2016 Fiji Under-20 representative will reunite with former teammates Temo Mayanavanua and Frank Lomani as he joins the Drua Vuvale.

The powerful tighthead says the opportunity was the result of years of sacrifice, perseverance and discipline, and he was looking forward to joining the squad and working towards the new season.

Drua General Manager Rugby Baden Stephenson says Ravuiwasa’s experience, physicality and strength would add valuable depth and competition to the front row.
